note: The backhand (5MH8RDf4qfg, The Padel School, seen from the net side, a close wide camera): the racket read by eye off head-centred cut-outs (2b-cutout-head.js; 180 px to the metre at the body's scale, y down; the follow-through's were cut at half 1.3 and are scaled to 180 here): B the hand on the handle, C the face's centre, w the head's apparent width over its real one, near +1 the tip plainly nearer the camera than the hand; the eighth number says which face the camera sees (-1 the back of the hand's, the one a backhand hits with: the ball is drawn over it at the contact). The camera is close, so the racket is drawn bigger than the body's scale in front of the body: lengths count only where near is set. Slow-motion parts used (a 100 fps camera at about 17 unique frames a second of 25: a frame in three is the one before again, dropped; the speed checked by the ball's fall against its own size): 69.56-72.16, 80.20-81.12, 91.12-94.24; contact the ball on the strings at 81.12. At the contact the camera looks well down on the racket (it is close and above it), so the head looks narrower than the face's real turn from the body's own line of sight: the widths either side of the contact are set for a face near upright (a flat drive, low to high), not as measured.
